title: Resource Transition
description: A platform-neutral normalized observation describing an actor causing or transporting a transition affecting a resource under a particular context, relative to available baseline information. This object records observed and normalized structure; it does not assign domain-specific intent, attribution, severity, or response.

extensions.description: Domain-specific or platform-specific extension data. Extensions must not redefine the semantics of canonical fields or introduce an unqualified domain verdict.

id.description: Unique identifier for this normalized transition event.

time.description: Time at which the underlying transition was observed or reported.

sequence.description: Optional monotonic sequence value supplied by the source or normalizer.

source.description: General source domain from which the transition was observed.

operation.description: Normalized operation associated with the transition.

native_operation.description: Optional platform-native operation name retained for diagnostic lineage.

phase.description: Processing phase represented by this event. Assessment and action phases belong to later schema-family objects.

correlation_id.description: Optional identifier used to associate this event with a broader activity, session, trace, or transaction.

id.description: Stable or locally stable identifier for the actor visible at the point of observation.

name.description: Optional human-readable or platform-derived actor name.

parent_ref.description: Optional reference to the parent or invoking actor.

role.description: Actor role relative to the transition. A transport actor may carry a change without originating it.

origin_actor_ref.description: Optional reference to a distinct actor believed or observed to have originated the transition. This reference does not independently establish attribution.

transport_actor_ref.description: Optional reference to a distinct actor that transported or propagated the transition.

state.description: Degree to which the actor identity is established.

publisher.description: Optional publisher, signer, owner, or responsible namespace associated with the actor.

instance_ref.description: Optional reference to the specific actor instance, process, session, application instance, model run, or equivalent.

account_ref.description: Optional privacy-preserving reference to the account or identity under which the actor operated.

state.description: Observed or externally supplied trust state. Trust does not establish that the current behavior is benign.

signed.description: Whether the actor carries a recognized signature when that concept applies.

basis_refs.description: References supporting the declared trust or reputation state.

id.description: Privacy-preserving identifier for the affected resource.

type.description: Structural type of the affected resource.

class.description: Limited shared classification of the resource. More specific classifications belong in extensions.

scope.description: Structural boundary within which the resource exists or is controlled.

protected.description: Whether the resource is subject to an established protection boundary. Null indicates that protection state is unknown.

canary.description: Whether the resource is intentionally used as a monitored decoy or early-warning resource. Null indicates that canary state is unknown.

recoverable.description: Whether a known recovery path exists for the resource. Null indicates that recoverability is unknown.

sensitivity.description: Structural sensitivity of the resource without exposing unnecessary identifying content.

location_ref.description: Optional local or privacy-preserving reference to the resource location. Raw sensitive paths should remain local when not required.

action.description: Normalized structural transition applied to the resource.

destructive.description: Whether the transition was directly observed to destroy or remove prior usable state. Null indicates that destructiveness is unresolved.

original_preserved.description: Whether the resource's prior state was preserved. Null indicates that preservation state is unresolved.

prior_state_ref.description: Optional reference to a recorded prior state.

resulting_state_ref.description: Optional reference to the resulting state.

reversibility.description: Observed or currently available reversibility of the transition. This field does not recommend a response.

entropy_shift.description: Observed or derived entropy change when applicable. Interpretation belongs to a downstream analyzer.

user_intent.description: Available evidence regarding user initiation or authorization. This field does not establish broader actor intent.

user_intent_ref.description: Optional reference to consent, interaction, command, workflow, or other evidence supporting the user-intent state.

interactive_session.description: Whether the transition occurred within an interactive session. Null indicates that session state is unknown.

bulk_operation.description: Whether the source or normalizer identified the activity as part of a bulk operation. Interpretation remains downstream.

network_origin.description: Whether the transition originated through a network boundary. Null indicates that origin is unresolved.

sync_transport.description: Whether synchronization infrastructure transported the transition.

origin_environment_ref.description: Optional reference to the environment in which the transition originated.

session_ref.description: Optional reference to the relevant user, application, agent, model, or system session.

scope_ref.description: Optional reference to the authorized observation scope under which the event was collected.

available.description: Whether relevant historical or expected-state information was available.

baseline_ref.description: Optional reference to the baseline object or history used for comparison.

role_coherent.description: Whether the observed transition is coherent with the actor's established structural role. Null indicates that this could not be determined.

comparison_refs.description: References to observations or histories supporting the baseline comparison.

state.description: Directly observed consequence of the transition. Domain interpretation belongs downstream.

affected_resource_refs.description: References to additional resources directly affected by this transition.

propagation_observed.description: Whether propagation beyond the primary resource was observed. Null indicates that propagation could not be determined.

recovery_impact.description: Observed effect on recovery state without assigning a broader risk score.

notes.description: Optional bounded description of directly observed consequences.

platform.description: Platform or source environment from which the observation originated.

adapter.description: Identifier for the adapter or normalizer that produced this event.

adapter_version.description: Optional adapter version associated with normalization.

capabilities_ref.description: Optional reference to the applicable tf.platform-capabilities declaration.

observed_at.description: Time at which the native observation was recorded.

normalized_at.description: Time at which the native observation was normalized into this schema.

native_event_ref.description: Optional local or privacy-preserving reference to the native event.

raw_event_retained.description: Whether the raw platform-native observation remains available under its original retention and privacy boundary.

derivation_refs.description: References to source objects or transformations used to produce this normalized event.

redactions.description: Classes of information removed or generalized during normalization.
